economic_picture.name: A broken part of a larger machine
economic_picture.body: Ardenia in March 1993 has an economy built for Union-scale demand and supply chains now divided by international borders. Output has fallen roughly forty per cent since 1989, and industrial output by more.

sectors.name: Industry
sectors.body: Zavost's plants were designed as pieces of a Union economy. Its nitrogen works is one of four plants in a supply chain whose other three now stand in Krasova. Enterprises retain workers on paper, miss wages in practice, and have lost the market they were built to serve.

sectors.name: Agriculture
sectors.body: The only growing sector owes its expansion to people farming for themselves after the collectives dissolved. Title, valuation and the claims of pre-1921 owners remain unresolved; many descendants are now diaspora supporters of the Liberal Democrats.

sectors.name: The informal economy
sectors.body: Customs at Tavri, fuel over the Krasovan border, cigarettes and metal through Vetrenka, and the capital's markets are not a marginal distortion. Something like a third of measured output and rather more employment live here, along with the money behind a dozen district seats.

kron.name: The kron
kron.body: Introduced in November 1992 at parity with the Union ruble, the kron has lost about ninety per cent of that value. Rubles still circulate in Zavost, while dollars and Krasovan notes circulate on Kelvet. Monthly inflation remains in triple digits and is falling, which is either a triumph or a rounding error depending on the briefing.

energy.name: Energy and the Zovar line
energy.body: Ardenia imports essentially all of its gas from Krasova through the Zovar transit line, under a Baran Council contract payable in hard currency the country does not have. The heating season runs October to March. Krasova has not turned the valve; it has mentioned the valve.

foreign_obligations.name: The ISF agreement
foreign_obligations.body: The Baran Council signed a stabilisation agreement with the International Stabilisation Fund in December 1992. Quarterly reviews cover the deficit and Bank independence; the budget already assumes disbursements that remain conditional.

foreign_obligations.name: The Concert
foreign_obligations.body: Ardenia has applied to the western economic bloc's association process and will not be admitted to it for a decade.

foreign_obligations.name: The Meridian Treaty Organisation
foreign_obligations.body: Its partnership programme is open to Ardenia; a security guarantee for a country with an active territorial dispute is not.

present_day.name: What March 1993 feels like
present_day.body: Power holds for most of the day in Vashtera and less in Duvinsk. The Chamber sits three days a week and achieves less than that. Two ministries have not paid staff since January. A currency-kiosk queue is the most reliable economic indicator available. Anera reports that all is normal, Tavri clears a container at a fifth of its declared value, and the ceasefire line exchanges ninety seconds of fire a week. This month the government can pay the Zavost wage arrears or the gas bill, not both.
